授業科目の概要.科目名称: Images of Japan across Contemporary East Asia
授業科目の概要.対象学部等: 学部2年 学部3年 学部4年
授業科目の概要.対象学年: 学部2年 学部3年 学部4年
授業科目の概要.授業科目に関する特筆事項: This class is taken by exchange students on the JTW class as well as by regular Kyudai students. The first session usually takes place on the Thursday before regular classes start for Kyudai undergraduates. Students who miss the first session will be able to 'catch up' by listening to the recording of the introductory lecture, which Prof. Vickers will distribute to all.

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）: This course discusses how Japan has been portrayed in post-war East Asia, and how visions of Japan in these societies have changed. In doing so, it analyses how the shifting portrayal of the Japanese ‘Other’ has influenced, or reflected, changing conceptions of national (or sub-national) ‘selves’ throughout the re-gion. Adopting a comparative perspective throughout, a principle focus of the course will be the societies of ‘Greater China’ (the mainland People’s Republic, Taiwan and Hong Kong) and the contrasting roles that Japan has played there in official and popular discourse on history and national identity. Other lectures will discuss the cases of Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines. While about half of the lectures will deal with the portrayal of Japan in school curricu-la and textbooks, extensive reference will also be made to other vehicles for public or popular culture, from museums and memorials to film and comics. By the end of the course, students will have a clearer sense of the historical, political and cultural forces and factors underlying the vastly differing attitudes to-wards Japan held by neighbouring countries across East and Southeast Asia.

授業科目の実施方法について.備考:
Note:
I will be sending out pre-recorded lectures for students to view before our regular weekly classes.
Each ‘live’ class will then involve discussion of the topic of the lecture. So, while listening to the lecture recordings, students are encouraged to try to think of comments and questions to share with the class.
The topics of the sessions are as follows:
Lecture 1: What can we learn from studying Japan’s role as ‘Other’ in East Asian societies?
General Overview and introduction to the project (Ch. 1)
The case of Singapore’s ‘Learn from Japan’ campaign (Ch. 2)
Lecture 2: Images of Japan in contemporary Hong Kong: schooling and popular culture (Ch. 8 and Vickers chapter in Remembering Asia’s World War Two)
Lecture 3: Japan in Taiwan’s School Textbooks (Ch. 9)
Lecture 4: Different perspectives on an East Asian hero: commemoration of Zheng Chenggong (鄭成功) in Taiwan, China and Kyushu (forthcoming book chapter by Vickers)
Lecture 5: Japan in Taiwanese and Chinese narratives of national history – the National Museum of Taiwan History compared with the National Museum of Chinese History (Vickers 2013)
Lecture 6: Japan in Chinese history textbooks (Ch. 7) – with specific reference to the case of Shanghai (Vickers and Yang 2013)
Lecture 7: The Sino-Japanese War in China’s public museums – reframing war memory to reflect China’s contemporary ‘rise’
Lecture 8: Commemorating wartime ‘comfort women’ - the case of China (Vickers 2019)
Lecture 9: Telling the story of the Japanese occupation in Singapore (Ch. 11)
Lecture 10: The war and occupation in Malaysian history textbooks (Ch. 10)
Lecture 11: Remembering war and occupation in the Philippines (Ch. 5 and Ch. 12)
Lecture 12: Japan in the public culture of South Korea (Ch. 6)
Lecture 13: Japan remembers its ancient and modern ties to Asia - a perspective from Western Japan (Kyushu and Yamaguchi)
Field trip to Hirado (July 13-14): The course will end with a field trip to Hirado (平戸), Nagasaki Prefecture, to attend the Koxinga Festival (鄭成功祭). 2024 is the 400th anniversary of the birth of Koxinga, who is celebrated in China and Taiwan for ‘liberating’ Taiwan from Dutch colonial rule. But Koxinga’s mother was Japanese, and he was born in Hirado, Kyushu.

授業科目の成績評価の方法について.レポート:
Students will be assessed mainly on the basis of a short essay or report in answer to one of the following questions:
The changing portrayal of Japan in other post-war East Asian societies reveals more about the politics and cultures of those societies than about ‘reality’ within Japan itself. Do you agree? Discuss with reference to at least two societies.
Write a critical review of two contemporary East Asian films (feature films or documentaries) that prominently feature depictions of Japan. Assess their significance in reflecting (or perhaps also shaping) the cultural and political climate in the societies that produced them.
Essays should be written in English and should be about 1,500 words long.
